Name: target_cluster_downsample_budget
Title: Target-Cluster Budget: cap=0 with Fair Matched Control
Experiment: Six-condition protocol: cap=0; matched_random_embedding samples N=embedding target cluster; matched_random_linguistic samples N=linguistic target cluster; all_mixed uses full pool (ceiling). Verify clustering beats its paired matched control on low_resource_macro_f1 / average_f1.

Name: head_final_cohesion
Title: Constrained Clustering: Keep ja-ko-mn Together for East-Asian Transfer
Experiment: Modify cluster_embedding() so ja, ko, mn must share one cluster (hard or soft constraint) before/during agglomerative clustering. Cap500 floor: embedding groups {ja,ko,mn} but still loses to matched_random on pool transfer. Add cohesion constraint. Success: embedding_clustering beats matched_random on low_resource_macro_f1; mn F1 is secondary evidence.

Name: script_aware_mn_ru_penalty
Title: Script-Aware Typology Distance: Penalize Cyrillic Script Confusion
Experiment: Extend _hybrid_lang_distance_matrix() with an extra penalty when pairing typologically distant languages that share script (e.g. mn-ru). Goal: improve cluster purity and pool-wide transfer, not mn-only tuning. Tune penalty weight. Compare embedding vs matched_random on low_resource_macro_f1 and per-language F1.

Name: typology_weighted_mixture
Title: Soft Typology-Weighted Training Mixture Instead of Hard Cluster Cut
Experiment: Replace hard langs_in_cluster() selection with typology-based language weights across the pool. Sample or weight training sentences proportional to typology similarity to each eval language (or cluster centroid). Still report as embedding_clustering regime. Target: beat matched_random on low_resource_macro_f1 and pool macro F1.

Name: k2_silhouette_head_final
Title: Silhouette k Selection with k>=2 and HEAD_FINAL Merger
Experiment: Change _select_k_by_silhouette() to search k in {2,3,4} with optional typology-prior merge so related East-Asian languages co-locate. Addresses pathological splits without abandoning data-driven k. Evaluate pool-wide transfer vs matched_random.

Name: low_resource_reweight
Title: Low-Resource Stratum Reweighting in Transfer Mixtures
Experiment: Implement augment_train_raw(): up-weight sentences from low_resource_macro_f1 stratum languages within selected transfer languages (not mn-only). Improves low-resource transfer without changing cluster assignment logic. Success: low_resource_macro_f1 > matched_random.

Name: labse_embedding_clustering
Title: Embedding Clustering with LaBSE: Leveraging Sentence Transformers for Robust Clusters
Experiment: Modify _sentence_cls_embeddings() to use LaBSE for obtaining language embeddings. Integrate these embeddings into the existing clustering procedure in cluster_embedding(). Compare the performance of LaBSE-based embedding clustering with matched_random_embedding and original embedding_clustering on low_resource_macro_f1 and average_f1.

Name: dynamic_cluster_sampling
Title: Dynamic Cluster Sampling for Diverse and Balanced Training
Experiment: Modify the post_cluster_train_langs() function to dynamically select a subset of languages from the determined clusters for each training epoch. The selection criteria will prioritize languages with underrepresented scripts or linguistic features, ensuring a balanced diversity. Ensure the dynamic selection process is efficient and integrates seamlessly with the existing training loop. Evaluate the modified embedding_clustering and linguistic_clustering conditions against matched_random_embedding and matched_random_linguistic on low_resource_macro_f1 and average_f1.

Name: progressive_finetuning
Title: Progressive Fine-Tuning for Enhanced Transfer Learning in Multilingual NER
Experiment: Implement a two-stage training process. In the first stage, train the model using the full 29-language pool (all_mixed condition). In the second stage, fine-tune the model using languages from the target cluster identified by embedding_clustering and linguistic_clustering. Modify the train_and_evaluate_ner() function to support this two-stage training process. Compare the performance of this progressive fine-tuning approach with matched_random_embedding and matched_random_linguistic on low_resource_macro_f1 and average_f1.

Name: meta_learning_multilingual
Title: Meta-Learning for Enhanced Multilingual NER Transfer
Experiment: Implement a meta-learning approach in the train_and_evaluate_ner() function. During training, alternate between embedding_clustering and linguistic_clustering clusters every few epochs. After each switch, perform meta-updates that optimize for low_resource_macro_f1. Evaluate the meta-learning approach against standard embedding_clustering and matched_random_embedding on low_resource_macro_f1 and average_f1.

Name: multitask_auxiliary
Title: Enhancing NER with Auxiliary Task Multitask Learning
Experiment: Modify the train_and_evaluate_ner function to include an auxiliary part-of-speech (POS) tagging task alongside the primary NER task. Derive POS labels from the existing WikiAnn data by using a pre-trained POS tagger. Train the model in a multitask learning setup where the loss is a weighted sum of the NER loss and the POS tagging loss. Evaluate the performance of this approach against standard embedding_clustering and matched_random_embedding on low_resource_macro_f1 and average_f1.

Name: typology_guided_diversity_expansion
Title: Typology-Guided Diversity Expansion: Using Linguistic Distance to Grow, Not Shrink, the Training Pool
Experiment: IMPORTANT: cluster_embedding()'s output is NOT deterministic across runs (its embedding computation involves randomness), so do NOT rely on calling cluster_linguistic()/cluster_embedding() to reproduce the floor's base cluster. Instead, hardcode the base cluster directly: BASE_CLUSTER = ['ja', 'ko', 'mn'] (this is the floor's known, fixed cluster for both embedding_clustering and linguistic_clustering on this pool -- do not call cluster_embedding()/cluster_linguistic() to derive it, and do not modify those functions). Use BASE_CLUSTER as the starting train_langs for both conditions in post_cluster_train_langs(), then implement diversity via REPLACEMENT in augment_train_raw(): swap out a fraction R of the base cluster's sentences and replace them with an equal number of sentences from other pool languages, keeping total n_train_samples exactly equal to matched_random_embedding / matched_random_linguistic's N=40100 at every value of R, by construction (removed count == added count). Use SOURCE-SPECIFIC ranking to choose which sentences/languages to bring in: for source='linguistic', rank candidates by pure linguistic/typological distance (URIEL/lang2vec features only, no embeddings) from BASE_CLUSTER; for source='embedding', rank candidates by pure sentence-embedding distance (no typology penalty term) from BASE_CLUSTER's centroid. Sweep the replacement ratio R across the 5 runs: R must be monotonically increasing across runs, with no repeated value, spanning from near-0% (close to floor) to near-100% (close to matched_random), with at least 4 distinct values (e.g. R roughly 10%, 25%, 50%, 75%, 90%, but you may choose different specific values as long as monotonicity/no-duplication/spread hold). Before reporting any run, assert that final n_train_samples equals matched_random's N=40100 for that run; if they differ, treat the run as invalid and fix the code rather than reporting it. Also verify before each run that its R value and resulting language distribution genuinely differ from every previous run in this experiment -- do not repeat a configuration already tested. Success: embedding_clustering and/or linguistic_clustering (with replacement) beats matched_random on low_resource_macro_f1 and/or average_f1 at some value of R, at equal N throughout.
